Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register using the *1 on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. Please stand by while registrations are processed. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Lena Novak, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; Emma Walsh, Chief Product Officer; and Tyler Brooks, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: average contract value trends, next quarter ARR guidance, sales efficiency, CAC trends, operating expense breakdown, churn analysis, and MRR trends.

These areas highlight our operational strength and path forward. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $210 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $45 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $850 million to $870 million.

To provide more color on the key areas Sarah highlighted, let me start with our average contract value metrics, which continue to reflect the strength of our land-and-expand model and the premium positioning of our CloudForge platform in the AI-driven DevOps and cloud observability market.

For Q3 FY2024, our overall ACV came in at $47,200, representing an 18% year-over-year increase from $40,000 in Q3 FY2023, and a solid 5% quarter-over-quarter improvement from $45,000 in Q2. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY ACV growth, underscoring our ability to drive higher value per customer amid a selective buying environment reminiscent of the post-2022 SaaS reset.

Breaking it down by cohort, new logo ACV—our average annualized value from net new customers—reached $58,500, up 28% YoY from $45,700. This acceleration is driven by a shift toward larger enterprise deals, with our top-tier ACV bucket (deals over $100K) now comprising 32% of new bookings, compared to just 18% a year ago. We're seeing this in wins like the recent $250K ACV expansion with a Fortune 100 financial services firm, layering on our ForgeAI predictive analytics module atop our core observability stack—similar to how Datadog has scaled with its AI dashboards.

For existing customers, ACV expanded to $44,800, a 14% YoY increase, fueled by our industry-leading 118% net revenue retention rate. Expansion revenue accounted for 42% of total bookings this quarter, up from 35% last year, primarily through cross-sell of high-ACV add-ons like our Autonomous Remediation engine and Kubernetes-native security suite. This mirrors trends at peers like Splunk pre-Cisco acquisition, where modular upsells have been key to ACV lift.

Regionally, North America remains our ACV powerhouse at $52,400—20% YoY growth—benefiting from deep integrations with AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI, which have enabled us to capture multi-cloud workloads in hyperscale environments. EMEA ACV grew even faster at 25% YoY to $42,100, propelled by our FedRAMP High and EU Data Boundary certifications, helping us close deals with regulated industries like a major European telco at $180K ACV. APAC, while still nascent at 12% of bookings, saw ACV surge 35% YoY to $38,900, driven by Japan and ANZ enterprise adoption amid cloud repatriation trends and partnerships with NTT and Alibaba Cloud.

Strategically, these trends are no accident. We've invested heavily in our "Forge Elite" enterprise motion, including AI-powered contract optimization tools that dynamically price based on usage telemetry—boosting realized ACV by 15% post-go-live. Pricing discipline has been pivotal too: selective 8-10% list price increases on premium tiers, coupled with outcome-based pricing pilots, have resonated in this era of CFO scrutiny, much like Snowflake's consumption model has premiumized its ACV.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 ACV to land in the $48,000-$49,000 range, with new logo ACV pushing toward $62,000 as we ramp our GenAI co-pilot launch at AWS re:Invent. Risks remain around elongated sales cycles in SMB—where ACV ticked down 2% QoQ to $12,500 due to budget constraints—but our focus on dollar-based net expansion keeps us insulated.

Overall, these ACV dynamics validate our thesis: in a maturing SaaS landscape with ARR multiples compressing to 7-9x for high-growth names, sustainable ACV expansion is the new rulebook for Rule of 40 dominance.

Turning now to our outlook for Q4 FY2024, which ends December 31st. We're pleased to provide guidance that reflects the continued strength of our core business, robust customer momentum, and the early traction from our strategic AI initiatives, all while navigating a macro environment where enterprise IT budgets are stabilizing but remain selective—much like we've seen at peers such as Snowflake and Datadog in their recent prints.

For Q4, we expect ending ARR of $528 million to $532 million, representing 24% to 25% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This compares to our Q3 ending ARR of $512 million, implying sequential growth of 3% to 4% quarter-over-quarter. To put this in context, this would mark our 11th straight quarter of at least 20% YoY ARR growth, outpacing the broader SaaS index which has hovered around 15-18% for large-cap names amid the post-pandemic normalization.

Breaking this down by key drivers, using the cohort analytics that our investor base knows well: We anticipate adding 85 to 95 new logos in Q4, weighted toward mid-market and enterprise accounts (average ACV of $450K), building on the 92 we landed in Q3. Our dollar-based net retention rate (DBNRR) is guiding to 112% to 115%, consistent with Q3's 114%, driven by multi-product adoption. Expansions now account for ~65% of our net new ARR, up from 60% a year ago, as customers deepen usage of our core CloudForge Analytics platform alongside our ForgeAI module—our generative AI copilot for real-time data insights, akin to how Salesforce's Einstein has boosted their Agentforce upsell cycles. We've seen particular strength in cross-sells to existing Tableau and Power BI migrants, with NRR in that cohort exceeding 120%.

Churn remains best-in-class at under 5% gross dollar churn for annual contracts, bolstered by our 98% renewal rate on expansion-eligible seats. Pricing discipline is intact; we implemented modest 5-7% uplifts on premium tiers in Q3 without material pushback, mirroring strategies at HubSpot and Zendesk.

A key tailwind is the ramp of ForgeAI, which contributed ~$12M of ARR in Q3 and is on track for $25M to $30M in Q4 as we roll out version 2.0 with agentic workflows and fine-tuned LLMs integrated via partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI. Early adopters—think Fortune 500 financials like a major bank automating compliance dashboards—are seeing 3x query throughput, driving land-and-expand velocity. We're also investing in zero-ETL data ingestion, reducing onboarding time by 40% compared to legacy tools like Looker, which positions us to capture share in the $50B BI market per Gartner.

Regionally: Americas (82% of ARR) expect 26% YoY growth, fueled by 15 net-new enterprise wins >$1M ACV, including expansions at two top-10 tech firms. US federal bookings via our FedRAMP High authorization are accelerating post-Q3's $8M quarter. EMEA (12% of ARR): 22% YoY growth, with GDPR-compliant AI features resonating; we're up 50% YoY in DACH region wins, partnering with SAP on co-sell motions. APAC (6% of ARR): 18% YoY growth, tempered by FX headwinds (JPY and AUD weakness) but offset by Japan enterprise logos and Singapore hub expansion. China remains nascent at <1% of ARR due to data sovereignty focus.

This guidance embeds ~$5M of favorability from easier comps versus last year's SMB slowdown, but assumes no major macro deterioration—like the budget scrutiny we've seen in Big Tech layoffs. Upside levers include faster-than-expected ForgeAI attach rates (targeting 30% of new ACVs) and our Q4 launch of industry packs for healthcare and retail, leveraging vertical AI models to boost win rates from 25% to 35% in pilots.

Risks to the guide include potential elongation in sales cycles (currently 90 days for enterprises) if capex freezes return, as flagged in recent ServiceNow commentary, or elevated churn from smaller seats amid remote work normalization. That said, our Rule of 55—calculated ARR growth plus EBITDA margin at ~58—remains firmly intact, underscoring efficient unit economics with payback <12 months.

Overall, this positions us for full-year FY2025 ARR growth of 23-25%, with raised conviction on our $1B ARR milestone by FY2026.

Next, our sales efficiency metrics continue to be a bright spot in our Q3 results, underscoring the leverage we're generating from our investments in product-led growth (PLG) and AI-enhanced go-to-market strategies. As many of you know, in the SaaS landscape—where companies like Snowflake and HubSpot have set the bar high—sales efficiency is all about compressing the sales cycle, boosting conversion rates across the funnel, and ultimately driving down customer acquisition costs (CAC) payback to under 12 months. We're thrilled to report meaningful progress here, even amidst a macro environment that's still pressuring enterprise budgets similar to what we've seen at peers like Salesforce and Workday.

Our average sales cycle across the board shortened to 92 days in Q3, down from 118 days in Q2 and a robust 22% year-over-year improvement from 118 days in Q3 last year. This is our shortest cycle in over two years, putting us in the top quartile for mid-market SaaS providers according to Bessemer Venture Partners' latest State of the Cloud report. Breaking it down by segment: Self-serve and SMB deals (under $50K ARR) closed in just 28 days on average, fueled by our freemium model and viral adoption loops akin to Notion's playbook. We saw 65% of these convert within 30 days of signup, thanks to in-app upsell prompts powered by our new AI recommendation engine, which suggests premium features based on user behavior—much like Zoom's early growth hacks. Mid-market ($50K-$250K ARR): down to 75 days from 95 days QoQ. This is where our inside sales team shone, leveraging Chorus.ai integrations for real-time call coaching, which improved demo-to-pilot conversion by 18%. Enterprise (over $250K ARR): the longest at 145 days, but even here we shaved 15 days off Q2 through targeted account-based marketing (ABM) campaigns. Wins like our $2.2M deal with a Fortune 500 healthcare provider closed in under 120 days by pre-qualifying intent signals from LinkedIn and 6sense.

Regionally, North America remains our efficiency powerhouse at 85 days average, benefiting from dense sales coverage and high intent from sectors like fintech and e-commerce. EMEA improved to 105 days, up 12% QoQ, driven by GDPR-compliant self-serve onboarding that accelerated pilots in the UK and Germany. APAC lagged at 130 days due to longer procurement cycles in Japan and Australia, but we're addressing this with localized pricing tiers and partnerships like our new integration with LINE for Southeast Asia workflows.

What’s driving this compression? Three key technical initiatives: First, AI-powered lead scoring via Salesforce Einstein and our proprietary CloudForge Predict—this dynamically prioritizes leads, reducing noise by 40% and focusing reps on accounts with >70% close probability. Second, virtual demo automation: our GenAI demo builder—similar to Gong's revenue intelligence but tailored for workflow SaaS—lets prospects self-run personalized demos, cutting live demo dependency by 55% and shortening mid-market cycles. Third, expanded PLG motion: 42% of Q3 bookings were PLG-attributed, with net revenue retention (NRR) hitting 128%, echoing successes at companies like Atlassian.

Turning to conversion rates, our funnel efficiency expanded significantly, with overall lead-to-closed-won improving to 8.2% from 6.1% QoQ—a 35% uplift. Marketing qualified lead to sales qualified lead conversion stood at 42%, up 9 points quarter-over-quarter and 15 points year-over-year, boosted by intent data from Bombora and content syndication via Demandbase. SQL to opportunity was 68%, up 5 points QoQ and 12 points YoY, thanks to inside sales expansion to 150 reps with AI scoring filtering out low-fit leads. Opportunity to close was 32%, up 6 points QoQ and 10 points YoY, driven by multi-threaded engagement via Outreach.io sequences emphasizing ROI calculators showing 3x productivity gains. Overall lead-to-won hit 8.2%, up 2.1 points QoQ and 3.5 points YoY—our magic quarter metric, with CAC payback now at 10.8 months.

Segment-wise, enterprise conversion held steady at 28% but with larger deal sizes ($450K average ACV), while SMB hit 15% overall thanks to self-serve. Regionally, North America led at 9.5%, EMEA at 7.8% (rising fast post-Brexit stabilization), and APAC at 5.9%—targeting 8% by year-end via Hindi/Mandarin sales pods.

Strategically, these improvements reflect our land-and-expand flywheel tailored to the SaaS workflow wars against incumbents like ServiceNow and Monday.com. We're doubling down on mid-market velocity to build ARR moats—aiming for 20% cycle compression in Q4 through further PLG investments, including a Slack-like channel partner marketplace launching next quarter. This positions us for rule-of-40 expansion, with sales efficiency contributing 15 points to our 68% score.

In summary, our sales engine is firing on all cylinders, delivering scalable growth in a tough IT spend environment.

Shifting to customer acquisition cost trends—a critical lever for our SaaS model here at CloudForge, where we're powering AI-enhanced collaboration platforms for mid-market and enterprise teams, much like how Slack revolutionized async comms but with our proprietary ForgeAI for real-time workflow automation.

CAC is calculated as our total sales and marketing expenses—covering everything from field sales commissions, ABM campaigns, performance marketing, content syndication, and partner enablement—divided by the number of new customers added in the quarter. Excluding one-time onboarding costs, this gives us a clean view of scalable acquisition efficiency. We're proud to report that in Q3, our blended CAC came in at $4,200, a 12% year-over-year decline from $4,770 in Q3 2023, and a modest 2% sequential improvement from $4,286 in Q2 2024. This marks our sixth straight quarter of CAC optimization, pushing our LTV/CAC ratio to a healthy 4.8x—up from 4.2x a year ago—and shortening our dollar-based payback period to 14 months, firmly in the elite tier for SaaS peers like HubSpot or Asana.

For new logos acquired in Q3, the median CAC was $3,950, skewed lower by our accelerating product-led growth motion. High-value enterprise deals, averaging $28K ACV, carried a higher CAC of $12,500 due to dedicated AE-led pursuits, but even there, we're seeing efficiencies. YoY, enterprise CAC dropped 18% as our inside sales team adopted AI-powered lead scoring via our own ForgeAI Insights tool, which has boosted pipeline velocity by 25%—similar to how Gong's revenue intelligence transformed outbound for sales orgs.

Segment trends tell an even stronger story. In our self-serve SMB segment—think startups and teams under 100 seats—CAC plummeted 28% YoY to just $1,850, driven by freemium upgrades. We hit 15,000 new self-serve customers in Q3, up 40% YoY, with viral coefficients climbing to 1.35 thanks to our Slack-like integrations with Zoom and Google Workspace, plus new TikTok and LinkedIn virality plays. This mirrors Zoom's explosive PLG scale during the pandemic but sustained post-hype. Conversely, mid-market CAC (100-500 seats) held steady at $6,200, reflecting heavier investment in partner ecosystems like our co-sell agreements with AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource, which contributed 22% of new mid-market logos at a blended 35% lower CAC.

Regionally, performance varied but trended positively overall. In North America, our core market at 68% of ARR, CAC fell 15% YoY to $3,900, fueled by inbound demand from our "AI Workflow Revolution" content series—over 2.5 million gated downloads via SEO and paid search, yielding a 4.2x ROAS on Google Ads. EMEA saw the biggest win, with CAC down 22% to $4,600, as GDPR-compliant PLG ramps and localization in German and French drove 55% YoY customer growth; our Dublin data center expansion helped here, reducing latency objections akin to Snowflake's regional edge wins. APAC remains a work in progress—CAC up 8% QoQ to $5,800 due to longer sales cycles and competition from local players like Lark—but we're countering with Tencent partnerships and Hindi/Japanese self-serve portals, targeting sub-$4,500 by year-end.

What’s powering these trends? A multi-pronged technical and strategic push: PLG acceleration now drives 42% of Q3 additions, up from 32% last year—we revamped our freemium tier with ForgeAI's no-code automations, achieving 18% conversion from trial to paid, best-in-class per Benchmarkit data, much like Notion's template virality. AI-driven sales efficiency: rolled out ForgeAI Sales Copilot internally, automating 60% of prospecting tasks, with our Magic Number hitting 1.4x and field sales productivity up 30%, win rates to 28% on ABM targets. Partner and ecosystem leverage: expanded our "Forge Partners Network" to 450 resellers, generating 28% of pipeline at 45% lower CAC, with key wins including integrations with Salesforce Einstein and ServiceNow. Marketing mix optimization: shifted 25% of budget to high-ROAS channels—performance max campaigns on Meta and LinkedIn returned 5.8x—while clawing back from underperforming SDR outbound. Churn on acquired cohorts is down to 3.2% monthly, validating quality.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 CAC to land between $4,000-$4,200, with continued pressure from PLG scale and Black Friday trial spikes. Full-year blended CAC should decline 14% YoY, supporting our Rule of 50% trajectory at 58% for FY24. Risks include macro headwinds like delayed enterprise budgets—echoing Q3 Salesforce guidance—but our 85% gross margins give us flexibility to invest without compromising efficiency.

These CAC trends underscore CloudForge's maturation into a capital-efficient SaaS leader. We're not just acquiring customers; we're building a moat through AI-native PLG, shortening payback, and expanding regionally. This positions us for 32% revenue growth in FY25, with expanding margins.

Now, on our operating expense breakdown for the quarter. Overall, total non-GAAP operating expenses came in at $145 million, up 18% year-over-year but flat sequentially from Q2. As a percentage of revenue, op-ex declined to 72% from 78% a year ago, reflecting strong operating leverage as our ARR surpassed $950 million—driven by 28% YoY revenue growth and 112% NRR. This puts us firmly on track for Rule of 40 attainment in FY2024, with growth plus margin now at 68 points.

R&D expenses were $68 million, or 36% of revenue, down from 39% YoY. R&D remains our largest opex bucket, underscoring our commitment to product-led innovation in a hyper-competitive SaaS landscape. Expenses grew 15% YoY, or about $9 million, but moderated sequentially due to efficiencies in our offshore engineering hubs. Key drivers include AI and GenAI initiatives—we accelerated investments in our Nexlify Intelligence platform, rolling out agentic AI workflows akin to Salesforce's Agentforce or ServiceNow's Now Assist. This quarter, we shipped multimodal capabilities—processing unstructured data like PDFs and videos—for our core CRM and workflow automation modules, boosting feature adoption by 25% among enterprise customers. Roughly 40% of the YoY increase, or $3.6 million, went toward these efforts, including fine-tuning our proprietary LLMs on customer datasets for vertical-specific use cases in healthcare and financial services. We also continued technical debt reduction and cloud optimization, refactoring our microservices architecture on Kubernetes and migrating 70% of our workloads to AWS Graviton instances for 30% better cost-performance, supporting our multi-cloud strategy with growing integrations into Azure and Google Cloud to win deals against incumbents like Workday and Oracle. Headcount grew modestly by 12% YoY to 850 engineers, with 60% now in cost-effective regions like India (Bangalore hub) and Poland (Krakow), where we leverage talent density for NLP and cybersecurity R&D. This mix kept average fully loaded engineer costs at $180K, below the U.S. SaaS peer average of $250K. Looking ahead, we expect R&D to stabilize at 34-36% of revenue in Q4, as AI roadmap milestones—like zero-ETL data pipelines—drive upsell velocity and reduce churn. These investments are already paying off: product-qualified leads from our free-tier AI beta surged 40% QoQ, contributing to a 15-point NRR lift from expansions.

Sales & Marketing expenses were $52 million, or 27% of revenue, down from 32% YoY. S&M expenses rose 12% YoY but declined 5% sequentially, as we leaned into high-ROI channels amid lengthening enterprise sales cycles—now averaging 9 months versus 7 last year, per our internal CRM data. This efficiency reflects a maturing go-to-market engine, with core sales efficiency improving to 1.8x (revenue per sales rep, up from 1.4x). Demand generation and CAC discipline: digital-led efforts, including ABM campaigns on LinkedIn and SEO for 'AI workflow automation,' accounted for 55% of new logos. CAC stabilized at $28K, flat YoY despite competitive pricing pressures from HubSpot and Pipedrive expansions. We realized $4 million in savings by optimizing paid search bids with our own ML-driven attribution model. Enterprise and partner ecosystem focus: 65% of ACV bookings came from Fortune 1000 deals, fueled by our AWS Marketplace presence—now generating 20% of pipeline, similar to Snowflake's channel momentum. Key wins included a $15M multi-year contract with a Big Four consultancy for EMEA rollout. Regionally, North America remains 75% of bookings, but EMEA grew 35% YoY to $120M ARR run-rate, driven by GDPR-compliant AI features. APAC lagged at 8% of total, prompting a $2M ramp in Singapore-based AEs to counter Zoho and regional players. Events like Dreamforce and our Nexlify Summit yielded a 4x pipeline ROI. Forward guidance: S&M as a percentage of revenue should trend to 25-27% in FY2024, supported by 120%+ NRR and LTV/CAC expansion to 4.2x as we shift toward land-and-expand motions.

General & Administrative expenses were $25 million, or 13% of revenue, down from 15% YoY. G&A was our brightest spot for leverage, up just 5% YoY and down 8% sequentially, dropping to 13% of revenue—well below the industry median of 16% for $1B ARR SaaS peers like DocuSign or Zendesk. Scaling efficiencies: headcount grew only 3% to 320, with automation via our internal RPA tools handling 40% of procurement and compliance workflows. Stock-based compensation moderated to $8 million (32% of G&A), reflecting post-IPO grant vesting normalization. Strategic investments: $3 million went to cybersecurity hardening—implementing zero-trust architecture ahead of SEC cyber disclosure rules—and international tax structuring for our 25% EMEA revenue mix. Legal fees ticked up $1 million for IP portfolio expansion around 12 new AI patents. Regionally, we're realizing 15-20% savings from shared services in Dublin for EU ops, offsetting U.S. inflation pressures.

In summary, our op-ex profile demonstrates disciplined scaling: R&D fueling differentiation, S&M driving efficient growth, and G&A delivering leverage. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 22%, up 500 bps YoY, positioning us for 25%+ margins at $1.2B ARR next year.

Continuing with churn analysis, which remains a cornerstone of our financial health here at CloudForge. As a reminder, we're a leader in AI-powered workflow automation and collaboration SaaS for mid-market and enterprise teams, powering over 15,000 customers globally with our flagship CloudForge Platform—think seamless integrations with tools like Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and ServiceNow, augmented by our proprietary AI agents for task automation.

Our net revenue retention (NRR) held steady at 118%, down just 1 point quarter-over-quarter but up 3 points year-over-year, reflecting resilient expansion amid a tougher macro environment. Gross revenue retention came in at 92%, with logo churn at 4.2% annualized—well below the SaaS industry average of 7-8% for enterprise-focused players like us, per our Benchmarking SaaS report and Bessemer Venture Partners' benchmarks. Revenue churn was even lower at 3.1%, driven by minimal multi-year contract non-renewals, which accounted for only 0.8% of ARR at risk. Dollar expansion revenue offset 85% of churn, primarily from upsells like our new AI Workflow Pro module, which saw 28% adoption among existing customers, adding $4.2M in net expansion ARR this quarter alone.

Key drivers of churn, segmented rigorously using our internal churn attribution model, which tags 95% of lost ARR to root causes via post-churn NPS surveys, CSM exit interviews, and ML-powered usage telemetry: Macroeconomic pressures accounted for 42% of churned ARR—budget scrutiny remains the top culprit, echoing what we've seen industry-wide with peers like Zoom and Asana reporting similar headwinds; specifically, 65% of these losses were from SMB segments under $250K ARR, where finance teams cited cost optimization amid 5-7% average headcount reductions, with $2.1M in contraction from downgrades to our Essentials tier. Competitive displacement was 28%, where Microsoft Teams and Copilot integrations stole share in 52% of cases, particularly in EMEA where bundled Office 365 pricing undercut our standalone value prop; another 30% shifted to vertical specialists like Monday.com for marketing teams or Rippling for HR workflows. Onboarding and adoption friction was 18%—usage data showed 22% of churned cohorts had <30% seat activation in the first 90 days, often tied to complex integrations with legacy ERPs like SAP S/4HANA. Feature gaps and support escalations were 12%, primarily requests for deeper generative AI customization, where we lagged slightly behind UiPath's agentic RPA before our Q3 launch.

Regionally, North America (72% of ARR) had churn lowest at 3.5% annualized, buoyed by sticky Fortune 1000 accounts like our expanded deal with a major bank adding 150 seats. EMEA (18% of ARR) ticked up to 5.8% due to GDPR compliance costs and economic slowdown—UK and German DACH renewals slipped 2 points YoY amid inflation. APAC (10% of ARR) delivered our best at 2.9%, fueled by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS Tokyo and high demand for multi-language AI in Japan and India, where ARR grew 45% YoY despite currency volatility.

Trends are encouraging: YoY, we've reduced voluntary churn by 15% through proactive interventions, with contraction ARR dropping from 2.8% to 1.9%. Early signals from our Q4 pipeline show stabilization, as inflation cools and AI hype drives "SaaS consolidation" plays—customers rationalizing 3-5 tools into platforms like ours.

Our mitigation strategies are multi-layered, blending customer success, product innovation, and data science. We've invested heavily here, allocating 12% of opex to CSMs, achieving a 9:1 customer-to-CSM ratio. Predictive churn modeling: our ML platform, built on Snowflake and Databricks, scores 98% of accounts monthly using 47 signals—like login velocity, feature adoption (e.g., AI agent usage <20% triggers white-glove check-ins), and sentiment from Zendesk tickets; this flagged 1,200 at-risk accounts in Q3, recovering $1.8M ARR via 72% save rate—up from 65% last year. Onboarding overhaul: rolled out "ForgeFast," our 30-day AI-guided onboarding, reducing time-to-value by 40%; new cohorts now hit 65% activation vs. 45% historically, with A/B tests showing 22% lower churn. Expansion-first CS: 60% of CSMs' quotas tied to net ARR growth; we ran 450 "health checks" quarterly, surfacing upsell opportunities like bundling our AI Analytics add-on, which drove 35% of expansions. Pricing and packaging tweaks: introduced flexible "pay-per-agent" AI pricing, mirroring Snowflake's consumption model, which stemmed 25% of budget-driven churn; also launched industry packs (e.g., Financial Services Edition with SOC 2 Type II enhancements) to counter vertical competitors. Technical initiatives: deepened 150+ integrations via our API marketplace, including real-time Copilot hooks to neutralize Microsoft threat; our churn prediction model now incorporates external signals like LinkedIn layoffs data and GDP forecasts from the IMF.

Looking forward, we're targeting NRR expansion to 122% by FY25 end, with churn below 4%. Q4 pilots of "AI Retention Agents"—autonomous bots that proactively suggest optimizations—have already saved $450K in beta. In this SaaS landscape, where winners like ServiceNow maintain 95%+ gross retention through land-and-expand, our focus on usage-driven retention positions us to outpace the field.

Finally, on MRR trends, which continue to be the bedrock of our financial health here at CloudForge. Monthly Recurring Revenue—or MRR—is our north star metric in SaaS, reflecting the predictable, high-quality revenue stream from our cloud-native DevOps platform, including our core CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration tools, and our rapidly scaling AI-driven deployment automation suite.

For Q3 FY2024, ending September 30th, we delivered $28.7 million in ending MRR, marking a robust 48% year-over-year growth and 13% quarter-over-quarter growth. This builds on Q2's $25.4 million, Q1's $23.1 million, and represents our 11th straight quarter of sequential acceleration. To put this in context, our trailing 12-month ARR now stands at $344 million, up 46% YoY, positioning us firmly in the upper echelon of high-growth SaaS players like Datadog or GitLab during their inflection phases.

Breaking down the components: Ending MRR equals prior period MRR plus new logo MRR plus expansion MRR minus churn MRR minus contraction MRR. New logo MRR contributed $2.8 million in Q3, or about 10% of ending MRR, up 25% QoQ—driven by 47 net new enterprise logos, including marquee wins like a top-5 global bank adopting our platform for their Kubernetes estate and a leading e-commerce player similar to Shopify migrating from legacy Jenkins setups; our sales velocity here improved 18% thanks to our refined ideal customer profile targeting Fortune 1000 DevOps leads. Expansion MRR was the standout at $4.1 million, or 14% of ending MRR—our strongest quarter ever, up 35% QoQ; this reflects our classic land-and-expand motion, with customers starting with our free-tier developer tools and scaling to enterprise-grade features; NRR hit 118%, fueled by upsells into our new AI CodeGen module—which automates 40% of CI/CD pipeline scripting—and zero-trust security integrations compliant with FedRAMP High; we've seen cohorts from Q1 FY2024 expand by an average of 2.7x, akin to Snowflake's consumption-based upside during their early hyperscaler partnerships. On the downside, churn MRR was $0.9 million (3.1% annualized rate), and contraction MRR $0.7 million (2.4% rate), for a total dollar-based net retention of 115%—within our target of <8% gross churn, though we did see a slight uptick in SMB downgrades, about 15% of the churn, from macroeconomic pressures, mirroring what we've heard from peers like Atlassian.

A significant change to highlight: our consumption-linked MRR, tied to our usage-based pricing model launched last year, surged 62% YoY to $9.2 million (32% of total MRR). This is a game-changer, as it aligns incentives with customer scale—much like MongoDB's Atlas billing during cloud sprawl; we've embedded ML-based forecasting into our billing engine, reducing billing disputes by 40% and unlocking latent expansion.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse at 68% of MRR ($19.5M, +52% YoY), bolstered by hyperscaler co-sell motions with AWS and Azure. EMEA grew to 18% ($5.2M, +55% YoY), with GDPR-compliant features driving wins in financial services—think BNP Paribas-scale deals. APAC is our fastest grower at 14% ($4.0M, +28% YoY), though we saw a Q2 slowdown from yen volatility; Q3 reaccelerated via localization in Japan and India, where we're partnering with NTT for sovereign cloud deployments.

Strategically, these trends validate our "AI everywhere" pivot. We've invested heavily in technical initiatives like our ForgeAI agentic workflows, which integrate with GitHub Copilot and reduce deployment times by 60%, per internal benchmarks. This has boosted our product-led growth funnel, with 65% of new logos now self-serve. Looking ahead, we expect Q4 MRR growth to moderate to 11-12% QoQ amid seasonalities but accelerate into FY2025 as we roll out multi-cloud federation—addressing the fragmentation pain point that's top-of-mind for CISOs post-CrowdStrike outage.

In summary, our MRR trajectory reflects resilient demand for modern DevOps in an AI-accelerated world, with expansion as the durable driver. We're guiding to $30.5-31M ending MRR for Q4, implying 45%+ FY2024 growth.
